name: language-rooted-module-fqn
body:
A module's FQN is its language root followed by its module identity: `module-fqn = <language-id>.<module-identity>`, where `<language-id>` is the id the `lang_switch` record carried (the frontend's declared id — `rust`, `go`, `java`, `cpp`, `ts`, `js`, `csharp`, `py`, `md` — used verbatim, not a display name). Every language's module identity gains the root: Go module paths, Java packages, C++ namespaces, Rust crate/module paths, TS `pkg.relpath`, the Python dotted package names, and markdown path-derived modules.

This makes module FQNs collision-free by construction across languages: each language is a disjoint root namespace. It SUPERSEDES the bare (unrooted) module FQN forms (see `domain.value.module-fqn-prefix`): a Rust module `apg` renders `rust.apg`, a Python package `pkg.sub` renders `py.pkg.sub`, a markdown directory `/abs/docs` renders `md./abs/docs`, a TS module `@co/ui.src` renders `ts.@co/ui.src`.

Acceptance: a Rust module `apg.ingest` renders `rust.apg.ingest`; a Python package `pkg.sub` renders `py.pkg.sub`; a markdown directory module renders `md.<absolute-path>`; no Module FQN lacks its language root; two same-named modules in different languages (e.g. a Rust `apg` and a Python `apg`) render distinct FQNs and both survive.
